subject: outbrainsign

error_analyses.observable_characteristics: The implemented focus order moves from the first panel's "Get started link" to the second panel's "Enter the code input". In the screenshots, the first panel is the standard login form and the second panel is a two-factor authentication area shown to the right. The transition is directly present in the KFG and evaluated transitions, with source label 5/position 5 and destination label 6/position 6.
error_analyses.matching_criteria: A transition where focus moves directly from the last actionable item of one visible authentication subsection to the first field of the next visible authentication subsection, with consecutive meaningful positions but a visible shift between adjacent panels or sections.
error_analyses.possible_cause: Observed evidence shows a direct focus move between two visible authentication sections. A possible reason for the detector miss is that it may have treated this as a normal consecutive move because the inferred positions are adjacent (5 to 6), while the reference data labeled the section-to-section handoff as an LNF. That hypothesis is unverified because the evidence does not reveal the detector's internal rule logic.
error_analyses.supporting_evidence: Ground truth includes this exact transition. It is absent from original_predictions. navigation_order lists Get started link at position 5 and Enter the code input at position 6. KFG contains an edge from /html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/div[3]/div[1]/div[2]/a[1] to /html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/div[3]/div[2]/form[1]/ul[1]/label[1]/li[1]/input[1]. Screenshot shows these controls in neighboring login and two-factor areas.

error_analyses.observable_characteristics: Focus moves from "Forgot password? link" to "Get started link" within the first login area. navigation_order shows positions 4 and 5 respectively, indicating consecutive meaningful order. In the screenshot, both are small auxiliary links near the login form heading area and appear as logically adjacent secondary actions.
error_analyses.matching_criteria: A transition between two visible, nearby auxiliary links in the same section where implemented focus and inferred meaningful order are consecutive and there is no documented wrap, reversal, or skipped intermediate focus target in the KFG.
error_analyses.possible_cause: A plausible cause is that the detector over-relied on visual placement or DOM structure differences between the forgot-password link and the separately wrapped get-started link, flagging a cross-container move even though the reference data treats it as acceptable. This is a hypothesis only.
error_analyses.supporting_evidence: original_predictions contains this exact transition, but ground_truth does not. navigation_order places /label[3]/a[1] at position 4 and /div[2]/a[1] at position 5. KFG shows a direct TAB edge between them. evaluated_transitions classifies it as FP.

error_analyses.pattern_hypothesis: Sparse support-link row with tolerated omission
error_analyses.observable_characteristics: The implemented sequence jumps from "Troubleshooting guide link" to "Contact support link". navigation_order gives positions 12 to 14, so the intervening meaningful position 13 is "Authenticate via email link". However, ground truth does not label this exact move as an LNF, even though a similar jump from position 11 to 13 is labeled. These links appear as a cluster of secondary support options beneath the two-factor login button.
error_analyses.matching_criteria: A transition within a dense cluster of low-priority support links where the implemented order bypasses another link in inferred order, but the reference data does not treat that specific bypass as a violation.
error_analyses.possible_cause: The detector likely flagged the non-consecutive inferred positions (12 to 14) inside the support-link cluster. The false positive suggests that positional-gap logic alone was insufficient because the reference evaluation may tolerate some reordering within this secondary link group. The exact rationale of the reference label cannot be established from supplied evidence alone.
error_analyses.supporting_evidence: original_predictions includes this transition; ground_truth does not. navigation_order: Troubleshooting guide link is position 12, Authenticate via email link is position 13, Contact support link is position 14. KFG includes a direct edge from /div[1]/div[2]/a[1] to /div[1]/div[4]/a[1]. Screenshot 2 shows multiple small links grouped below the orange Log In button.

error_analyses.observable_characteristics: Focus moves from the last support link in the two-factor area, "Authenticate via email link," to the first footer control, the "Outbrain footer logo link." navigation_order shows positions 13 to 16, but KFG confirms this is the implemented next step. The screenshots show the footer links aligned along the bottom after the authentication module.
error_analyses.matching_criteria: A transition from the last reachable control in a functional content module to the first footer link, with no additional implemented focus targets between them in the KFG for that state.
error_analyses.possible_cause: A likely cause is that the detector interpreted the large positional jump or the visual shift from main content to footer as an LNF. The reference data appears to accept this handoff because the implemented sequence simply exits the module into the footer. This remains a hypothesis about detector behavior.
error_analyses.supporting_evidence: original_predictions contains this transition; ground_truth does not. KFG shows a direct TAB edge from /html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/div[3]/div[2]/form[1]/ul[1]/div[1]/div[3]/a[1] to /html[1]/body[1]/footer[1]/div[1]/div[1]/a[1]. navigation_order places these at positions 13 and 16. Screenshot 2 shows footer links after the main authentication content.

error_analyses.observable_characteristics: Focus moves from "Contact support link" to "Go back link" within the two-factor section. navigation_order places them at positions 14 and 15, so they are consecutive in inferred order. The screenshot shows both as small text links below the main two-factor controls, with "Go back" visually set below the row of other support links.
error_analyses.matching_criteria: A transition between consecutive inferred positions inside the same visible feature area where the source is a support/help link and the destination is a local navigation or return link placed nearby below or after the support cluster.
error_analyses.possible_cause: A plausible explanation is that the detector did not flag the move because the meaningful positions are consecutive and the controls are within the same secondary-link area, while the reference data labels it as an LNF. The supplied evidence does not establish why the reference treats this as a failure, so the error mechanism is uncertain.
error_analyses.supporting_evidence: ground_truth includes this exact transition; original_predictions do not. navigation_order lists Contact support link at position 14 and Go back link at position 15. KFG contains a direct edge from /div[1]/div[4]/a[1] to /div[4]/a[1]. Screenshot 2 shows both links in the lower part of the two-factor module.

error_analyses.pattern_hypothesis: Text-link cluster jump after primary action loop
error_analyses.observable_characteristics: Focus moves from "Resend code link" to "Troubleshooting guide link." navigation_order shows positions 7 to 12, spanning multiple inferred positions including checkbox, label, login button, and another support link. KFG confirms this direct edge. In the screenshot, Resend code is aligned near the code input, while Troubleshooting guide is in the lower support-link row.
error_analyses.matching_criteria: A transition from an inline helper link near a form field to a later support link cluster, where several visible controls with meaningful positions intervene and the KFG still shows a direct TAB edge.
error_analyses.possible_cause: The detector may have missed this because both endpoints are links, or because it modeled the two-factor section as a secondary cluster and underweighted the long jump across mixed control types. This is a hypothesis; only the existence of the direct edge and the ground-truth label are observed.
error_analyses.supporting_evidence: ground_truth includes this transition; original_predictions do not. navigation_order places Resend code at position 7 and Troubleshooting guide at position 12, with positions 8 to 11 occupied by checkbox, label, button, and Use authentication app link. KFG shows a direct TAB edge from /label[1]/li[1]/div[1]/a[1] to /div[1]/div[2]/a[1].

error_analyses.observable_characteristics: Focus moves from the focusable "Trust this device label" to the "Two-factor Log In button." navigation_order shows positions 9 to 10, consecutive in inferred order. The checkbox itself is listed at position 8 and receives focus separately elsewhere, indicating a nonstandard grouping where label and checkbox/button are individually focusable in an unusual order.
error_analyses.matching_criteria: A transition where a focusable label within a checkbox/control group is followed directly by a submit button, with consecutive inferred positions but an unusual control grouping that may still be labeled problematic in the reference data.
error_analyses.possible_cause: The detector likely treated this as acceptable because the positions are consecutive and there is no apparent skipped implemented target. The reference data nevertheless labels it as an LNF, possibly due to the unusual separation of checkbox, label, and button order. That causal interpretation is unverified.
error_analyses.supporting_evidence: ground_truth includes this transition; original_predictions do not. navigation_order lists Trust this device label at position 9 and Two-factor Log In button at position 10. KFG shows a direct TAB edge from the label to the button. Screenshot 2 places these controls around the trust-device option and the orange Log In button.

error_analyses.observable_characteristics: The reference data labels the virtual Browser boundary entering the page at the "Username or Email input" as an LNF. KFG special nodes define this same input as v_0 and v_entry. No ordinary DOM source exists because the source is the virtual browser boundary. Screenshot 1 shows the input as the first focusable item in the login form.
error_analyses.matching_criteria: A transition whose source is the virtual Browser boundary rather than a DOM node, and whose destination is the first focusable element recorded as page entry.
error_analyses.possible_cause: A likely reason is that the original detector did not generate or score virtual browser-boundary transitions the same way it handled DOM-to-DOM transitions. This is supported by the absence of any Browser-source transition in original_predictions, but the exact implementation detail is not directly observed.
error_analyses.supporting_evidence: ground_truth includes the exact Browser -> input transition. evaluated_transitions marks browser_boundary as True. KFG v_special identifies /html[1]/body[1]/main[1]/div[3]/div[1]/form[1]/ul[1]/label[1]/li[1]/input[1] as v_0 and v_entry. original_predictions include only DOM-to-DOM transitions.

correct_transition_examples.relevant_characteristic: Comparable within the two-factor form: a detected LNF moving from the code input into the trust-device control group.
Comparable long jump from primary action back to an earlier helper link, useful against the missed Resend code -> Troubleshooting guide jump.
Comparable move from trust-device controls into the lower support-link cluster.
Comparable wrap/reentry inside the two-factor area, showing that some transitions around the secondary links were correctly detected.
Useful comparison for the FP Forgot password? -> Get started transition because it shows accepted sequential movement among nearby controls in the first login section.

subject_summary: This subject mixes a standard login panel, a two-factor panel, and footer links in one focus sequence. Several detector misses involve two-factor transitions that ground truth labels as LNFs even when inferred positions are consecutive, making the failure mechanism partly ambiguous from supplied evidence alone. The clearest FPs are normal adjacent movements between nearby auxiliary items or from the end of the module into the footer. The clearest FN is the Browser entry transition, which likely reflects special handling of the virtual boundary.
